text:
maya: quick kickoff 1: want to lock the benchmark story for the launch post and webinar. leaning into a 'tail-first' framing: show how optimizing for 95/99 reduces user-visible slowdowns and lowers cost after batching.

rafael: sounds strong. two asks: 1) make the hero causal (show same model + config, two outcomes), 2) give a tiny methodology footnote so readers trust numbers.

jo: user slices to use? my vote: help chat (very short), meeting notes (longish), code-assist (bursty qps). three is a nice cross-section.

camila: design constraints: 1 hero with two panels (latency CDF tails on left, effective $/response on right). use max 3 color accents. keep alt text and mobile-chops in mind.

tanya: marketing copy idea: head: "Predictable tails. Lower bills." subhead: "Same model. Better serving. Real savings when it matters."

maya: nice. rafael, can you draft the before/after numbers? we'll need avg/p95/p99 and $/1k for each slice. also show the delta after enabling auto-batching + prefix-cache + small-quant.

rafael: here's a quick synthetic extract from the perf run (us-east1, small kv enabled). raw CSV: 

```
segment,avg_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,cost_per_1k_raw,cost_per_1k_opt
help-chat,100,260,420,$10.0,$6.2
meeting-notes,460,980,1600,$32.5,$19.1
code-assist,85,210,390,$13.8,$9.0
```

jo: that looks credible. headline claim idea: "Up to 41% lower cost while hitting a 95th latency SLO" 1 helps if we pick the worst-case slice for the percent.

camila: visuals: left panel is a compact CDF showing p50/p95/p99 ticks for each slice (stacked small multiples). right panel is two grouped bars per slice: raw vs optimized ($/1k). add a tiny waterfall below the bars listing contributors: batching, prefix cache, perf-tuned kernels.

anna-brand: social blurb options: A) "Cut costs, not SLAs. See how we keep 95th latency tight while shaving run costs." B) "Make performance predictable. Make pricing sensible." both under 120 chars. include webinar link and signup CTA.

ci-bot: perf pipeline finished for run/4898702. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/perf/4898702 :white_check_mark:

maya: plan & owners: rafael cleans numbers + methodology note (EOD Tue), camila makes two hero mocks (Wed AM), jo drafts blog skeleton + appendix (Wed PM), anna-brand polishes social and alt text (Thu). webinar signup + poll: tanya owns creative and segmentation.

rafael: methodology note: we used same model weights, identical seq-limits, warmed KV cache, and simulated realistic QPS profile. will add raw logs link.

jo: appendix to include a 3-line explain: 1) what tail latency means for users, 2) how batching and cache change token accounting, 3) reproducibility steps + link to perf artifact.

camila: small accessibility ask: export hero PNG at >=1200px wide, include high-contrast variant and simple legend.

maya: experiment idea: put a micro CTA in the blog to run a 2-minute perf demo (hosted sandbox) that runs a quick inference on their prompt and reports p95 + cost estimate. route leads who run it >50% likely to sales nurture.

anna-brand: love that. shortened CTA: "Run a 2-minute perf check" with microcopy under the button: "No credit card, instant insights."

tanya: poll for webinar signups: "Which matters most? Lower tail latency / Predictable throughput / Lower cost" 1 will wire poll answers into lead tags.

rafael: i'll publish the cleaned CSV and sample chart data to the perf artifact and share links in the doc.

maya: great. sync Thurs 9am for final preflight. small reminder: avoid 'narrow' claims 1 keep wording defensible.

camila: noted. will keep numbers labeled as 'measured on workload X' and show the config in appendix.

maya: awesome team. thanks, see you Thu 9. :sparkles:
